item.title: Fortran in 2026: LFortran vs Flang vs gfortran — Which Compiler Should You Actually Use?
item.description: Fortran is 69 years old, and it is still the language that produces the weather forecast you read this morning, the finite-element stress numbers behind every bridge inspection, and a large share of the world’s climate simulation output. The language never lost its job. What did change — quietly, over the last three years — is the toolchain around it. In 2026 you no longer have exactly one realistic compiler choice, and that is genuinely new.
